messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT detected: GPU serving queue growth + autoscaler failing to add nodes. metric: gpu-queue-length > 1200 for 6m, autoscaler errors: registerBackoff and AssumeRole denied. Paging oncall.
sarah: oncall here, seeing a bunch of pod Pending due to insufficient GPU resources. digging into autoscaler logs now.
mike: autoscaler logs -> AWS STS AssumeRole failing for nodegroup-provision role: "AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole". Also a steady stream of 'register backoff: reconcile failed' messages.
lina: hmm we rotated infra credentials for the provisioning service earlier today, maybe the new role arn wasn't propagated to the autoscaler config. checking terraform state + k8s secret.
jonathan: confirmed: autoscaler still using old role arn (arn:aws:iam::111:role/gpu-provision). TF shows new role arn: arn:aws:iam::111:role/gpu-provision-v2. Provisioning service recently moved to cross-account execution, probably missed update.
sarah: we need a mitigation path fast. two options: 1) fallback traffic to Dedicated cluster (low latency customers only?) or 2) manually create nodepool with existing instance profile to drain queue. thoughts?
oncall-ops: customer-impact: some realtime inference requests are hitting 500s or queueing for >2s. internal SLOs degrading; recommend external status msg in 10m if we don't have stable mitigation.
mike: manual nodepool create looks fastest. I'll spin up a small GPU nodegroup (3 g4dn) with instance-profile that has current passRole perms. run: ```aws eks create-nodegroup --cluster-name prod-gpu --nodegroup-name tmp-hotfix --scaling-config minSize=0,maxSize=3,desiredSize=3 --instance-types g4dn.xlarge --node-role arn:aws:iam::111:role/gpu-provision-v1```
lina: watch the taints - our admission controller enforces gpu:reserved=true on managed pools. if we create nodes with different taint keys pods might not schedule. include tolerations on the deployment or set taint to match.
jonathan: trying manual creation now. if nodes join but don't register, we'll still see registerBackoff.
cory: quick note: if this is cross-account passRole, the instance profile also needs sts:AssumeRole permission for the target role. double-check trust policy.
mike: nodes came up but we have kubelet errors: "taint key mismatch: expected gpu-reserved but found gpu_reserved" — weird naming convention mismatch from a previous config migration.
sarah: okay fix path: 1) update provisioned nodegroup launch config to use correct taint key (gpu-reserved) and instance profile; 2) patch pending pods to add toleration for gpu_reserved temporarily OR create a short-lived patch on node taints to match. I'm going to patch pods with toleration to get immediate scheduling.
lina: patch applied to critical deployments. pods starting to schedule, queue length dropping.
oncall-ops: incident-bot escalated to SE team and prod-support. preparing customer update: "Experiencing degraded inference throughput due to GPU capacity provisioning failure. Mitigation in progress; traffic routed and scaling being exercised. ETA 30-45m."
mike: adding follow-up: create a runbook ticket to reconcile role arn propagation in TF pipeline and a postmortem for the credential rotation step. Also recommend guardrail: fail autoscaler to read-only if role check fails so we get earlier alert.
sarah: agreed. I'll own the postmortem. for now monitoring shows queues returning to baseline, keeping page open for 30m. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (nodes added, workloads scheduled). escalation cleared."
